title: Quantitative whole-slide image analysis of CD3 and CD8 immunohistochemical stains
author: Seungyeon Yoo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yqvfvw6

steps.title: Initialize Project Scripts
steps.instruction: Set up the script environment by executing the batch file to generate necessary directory substitutions.

substeps.instruction: Open the 'code' folder and double-click 'run.bat' (Windows users).
For non-Windows users, manually perform the following substitutions and move files to Project/Scripts: replace _REPLACE_DIR_ with /Data/ and _REPLACE_PROJECT_DIR_ with /Project/.

steps.title: Annotate Tumor Area
steps.instruction: Manually define the tumor area using the polygon tool in QuPath.

substeps.instruction: Select the polygon tool, click one point, and drag along the contour of the tumor area; double-click the finishing point to close the contour.
Include acellular mucin pools in mucinous carcinoma.
Exclude adenomatous areas, normal mucosa, necrotic debris, tissue folding, speckles, peritumoral lymph nodes, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue.

steps.title: Create and Refine Tiles
steps.instruction: Generate tiles to further elaborate the tumor area.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Analyze > region identification > create tiles.
Delete or move tiles as needed to refine the tumor area.

steps.title: Define Invasive Margin (IM)
steps.instruction: Identify the tiles that constitute the invasive margin.

substeps.instruction: Hold the Ctrl key and click tiles that constitute the IM.
If the mucosa-to-serosa axis is evident, define IM as the 'frontmost' files (excluding tiles approaching the mucosa).
If the axis is not evident, consider any border with non-neoplastic tissue as the IM.
Ensure IM tiles contain tumor cells; exclude tiles bordering abscess, necrosis, or lymph nodes.

steps.title: Save IM Annotations
steps.instruction: Run the first Groovy script to save screenshots of highlighted IM tiles and tile objects.

substeps.instruction: Select Automate > Show script editor.
Select File > Open and open '1.groovy' from the project's script folder.
Execute the script by selecting Run > Run or pressing Ctrl+R.

steps.title: Perform Cell Identification and Superpixel Segmentation
steps.instruction: Process all project images to identify putative cells and segment images into superpixels using the second Groovy script.

substeps.instruction: Open '2.groovy' in the script editor.
Select Run > Run project (without save).
In the resulting window, click '>>' to select all images in the project and click [OK].
Verify that four subfolders (Cell_before_data, Cell_before_qpdata, SP_before_data, SP_before_qpdata) are created in the data folder and populated with N files.
Check SP_before_data and SP_before_qpdata for files with oddly small sizes (indicating superpixel segmentation failure); if found, repeat steps 3 through 6 for those specific files.

steps.title: Filter Lymphocytes and Classify Superpixels
steps.instruction: Run an external Python/R pipeline to filter true lymphocytes and classify superpixels into tumor or stroma.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the R directory is in the system environmental variable and that R packages 'readr', 'caret', and 'randomForest' are installed.
For Windows users with Anaconda, open Anaconda Powershell Prompt and execute: 'python /3.py'.
Note: The script classifies all cells as positive for CD3 stains but applies a specific lymphocyte classifier for CD8 stains to filter nonspecific membranous staining.

steps.title: Apply Cell Filtering Results
steps.instruction: Import the filtered cell results back into QuPath.

substeps.instruction: Open '4.groovy' in the script editor.
Select Run > Run for project (without save).

steps.title: Apply Superpixel Classification
steps.instruction: Apply superpixel classification to obtain intraepithelial and stromal TIL.

substeps.instruction: Open '5.groovy' in the script editor.
Select Run > Run for project (without save).
Verify results by navigating to the data folder > 'ES_Tilewise_qpdata' subfolder and opening any qpdata file.

steps.title: Generate Final Quantitative Data
steps.instruction: Execute the final Python script to produce the quantitative measurement file.

substeps.instruction: For Windows users with Anaconda, open Anaconda Powershell Prompt and execute: 'python /6.py'.
The output will be a file named 'count.csv' containing 207 measures for each case.
